summary: H.R. 9706, titled the 'Facial Recognition to Protect Children Act', requires operators of wagering and prediction market platforms to use commercially available facial recognition technology to verify that users are over 18 years of age. It limits data collection to what is necessary for age verification and mandates the deletion of unnecessary data. The Federal Trade Commission is tasked with enforcement. The bill also amends the Commodity Exchange Act to grant the Commodity Futures Trading Commission additional oversight and authority regarding event contracts, including prohibiting certain event contracts contrary to the public interest, regulating promotional communications and anti-money laundering programs, establishing an Advisory Council on Consumer Protection, and creating an Office of the Retail Advocate.

affected_groups.effect: Must undergo facial recognition scanning to prove they are over 18 before accessing platforms and placing wagers or orders.
affected_groups.group: Users of wagering or prediction market platforms

affected_groups.effect: Must implement facial recognition age-verification technology, comply with data minimization and deletion rules, and face potential FTC enforcement for non-compliance.
affected_groups.group: Wagering and prediction market platform operators

affected_groups.effect: Given the authority to enforce age-verification requirements and promulgate necessary regulations.
Given expanded responsibilities to review event contracts, enforce anti-money laundering and fund segregation rules, establish an advisory council, and set up an Office of the Retail Advocate.

key_provisions: Wagering and prediction market platform operators must verify user age using commercially available facial recognition technology to ensure users are older than 18.
Operators are prohibited from collecting, processing, or transferring user biometric data beyond what is strictly necessary for age verification, and must delete unneeded data.
Violations of the age verification requirement are treated as violations of Federal Trade Commission regulations regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission may determine that event contracts involving unlawful activities, terrorism, assassination, war, violence, or gaming are contrary to the public interest and prohibit them.
Derivatives clearing organizations offering event contracts must maintain anti-money laundering programs, proper fund segregation, and abide by restrictions on deceptive promotional communications.
Establishes an Advisory Council on Consumer Protection within the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to study retail participation and consumer protections.
Establishes an Office of the Retail Advocate within the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to assist retail participants, analyze regulations, and report annually to Congress.
missing_information: Specific timelines or effective dates for when platforms must implement the facial recognition technology.
Exact details on the financial penalties the FTC may assess beyond general reference to the FTC Act.
